## This document shows how to use functions and apply it to data for various graphs

```{r}

library(tidyverse)

years <- 2001:2026 ## Set years

Employee.Info <- setNames(
  lapply(years, function(y) {
    read.csv(paste0("Employee_", y, ".csv"))
  }),
  years
)

```

## Graph Generator Function
```{r}

## The column name in excel (category.year)

plot_employee_data <- function(data, year, category, x_label, title_label, top_n = 10) {
  
    col_name <- paste0(category, ".", year)
    col_sym  <- sym(col_name)
    
    count_df <- data %>%
      filter(!is.na(!!col_sym)) %>%
      count(!!col_sym) %>%
      slice_max(n, n = top_n)
    
    ggplot(count_df, aes(x = fct_reorder(!!col_sym, n, .desc = TRUE), y = n)) +
      
      geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
      coord_flip() +
      labs(
        x = x_label,
        y = "Number of Employees",
        title = paste( "Number of Employees by", title_label, "(", year, ")")
      )
}

```

## Job Title Graphs
```{r}

job_plots <- lapply(years, function(y) {
  plot_employee_data(
    data = Employee.Info[[as.character(y)]], year = y, category = "Job.Title", x_label = "Job Title", title_label = "Job Title Graphs")
})

names(job_plots) <- years

for (p in job_plots) print(p)

```
